items.summary: One thing I noticed... About really bright minds... Is when you…
items.content_html:
One thing I noticed...

About really bright minds...

Is when you ask them a question...

...they pause...

Before answering...

You can see the gears turning...

...⚙...

I've known idiots who consider this low wattage.

But they're idiots for a reason.

Idiots.

Idiots respond so fast they cut the question off.

They think it's smart to do so.

But it's not.

It's the opposite.

Idiots.

So anyways, I'm going to start pausing when I answer now.

You have to do it almost to the point of discomfort.

The pause that is.

Furrowed brow.

Eyes distant.

Then wait a little bit longer.

Wait too long.

Then, and only then, answer.

Ideally, you'd do so with a poignant response.

Well thought out and pre-reasoned.

Several iterations inside your head.

But this is the ideal.

Not necessary.

The necessary part is to look like you're doing it.

...I might have that all wrong...

...

...

...

...But don't we all?...

🔄

items.title: Where Are You Going, Pilgrim?
items.summary: Say your arse got to Plymouth Rock. Back in the day.
items.content_html:
Say your arse got to Plymouth Rock.

Back in the day.

How far you moving out west?

You making it to the other ocean?

Or you stopping somewhere?

Somewhere in Nebraska.

Idaho, maybe?

Pocatello!!!

Or would you stay put?

It's dark in New Amsterdam.

Now, I ain't no pilgrim, Pilgrim.

Or am I?

[Looks up dictionary term:]

A pilgrim is a person who takes a long journey to a sacred or holy place for religious reasons.

This sounds like me.

Or, at least, I'd like it to.

I'd like it to sound like me.

Now, I ain't Chon Wang.

But I dig the Wild West.

Just wasn't for me.

Here you go.

Didn't find God there.

Almost lost Him.

Almost.

🙏

Your whole life is a pilgrimage.

If you think about it.

If you do it right.

A (hopefully) long journey.

To the most sacred places.

In full faith.

May we all get to where we're going.

I'd probably stop in Kansas.

items.title: Game In The Skin
items.summary: The most intolerant wins. You ever think about that? Now, I…
items.content_html:
The most intolerant wins.

You ever think about that?

Now, I consider myself a laid back fellow.

LOL.

Like a lot of us.

Most of us just doing our thing.

Minding our own.

You got a problem with that?

Well, you will probably win, then.

It's fooked up but that's why we're here.

Remember gluten free?

The thing is, most of it doesn't seem like a big deal.

So we shrug it off.

But it is.

I'm only inconvenienced.

It is the biggest deal.

Does this have seed oil?

Oh for the love of...

items.title: All I've Got Is An Autograph
items.summary: I bought a book the other day. You don't read. You…
items.content_html:
I bought a book the other day.

You don't read.

You barely listen.

Hey, it happens.

I like to buy ones you can't find digitally.

Oldish ones.

Obscurish ones.

Hidden gems.

And so I found one I already own, online but in analog form, and ordered it.

Two is one.

And it came in good shape.

Always a win.

And, surprisingly, it was autographed by the author.

Now if you buy a lot of tangible books intangibly, you'll notice this.

Signed copies.

Unmentioned.

At bargain rates.

Often, they are personalized.

To Milton,

Reach for the stars!

And sometimes, they're autographed by, not the author, but the gifter.

I don't really think of individual copies of books having their own unique stories but they do.

They have unreplicable tales.

Outside of its internal contents.

It has its own external contexts.

What was a print run of X number is really a unique 1 of 1.

With a story all its own.

And I suppose we're all like that.

Massive print runs, but really a one of one.

A unique take on an old story.

With our own personalized, autographed, version.

Hey Numbnuts,

Don't screw this up.

Love,

Al

[Thinking while staring at you intently.]

I'll give you...three dollars.

📕

🐆

items.title: Quill Over Key
items.summary: I got nothing to say. Yeah right. I don't. Nothing. Nada.
items.content_html:
I got nothing to say.

Yeah right.

I don't.

Nothing.

Nada.

Zilch.

When I write, by hand, with pen and paper, it's awesome.

Wonderful.

But there's a limit.

I'm limited by how fast, or slow, I can write.

I have to be deliberate.

Thoughts move a bit faster than my penmanship.

I have to slow down.

And so I learned to love typing.

I can almost type stream of consciousness here.

Meaning I can type as I think.

Before I think even.

Lord help us.

Just typing words out first to make a thought appear later.

And so when I handwrite, the output is thoughtful, considered, and concise.

When I type, woo boy, you get this.

Rambles.

It occurs to me, as such things do, that this musings column has halted my hand written stuff.

My offline musings.

Best musings are done offline.

All this (pointing to iterating) is a bit absurd.

Agreed?

Mmhmm.

Time to pick up that feather.

items.title: Unreasoned Within Reason
items.summary: I want to teach you a new term. Orthogonal bets. Oar.
items.content_html:
I want to teach you a new term.

Orthogonal bets.

Oar.

Thog.

Gonal.

Now, it may not be new to you, but if it is, it is.

Orthogonal is a fancy way to say 90 degrees.

Perpendicular.

Which is also fancy.

X goes up.

Y goes right.

Never the two shall cross.

I suppose they do at you, though.

You are the cross(roads).

I read it in two ways.

Maybe more.

One is if everybody zigging.

You zag.

Everyone zagging.

You zig.

You dig?

And if all you do is zag.

Maybe somethings you zig.

Or if zig, then zag.

If you Zig Ziglar.

Try Zag Zaglir.

You can call it a hedge, I suppose.

Hedge on your life.

If you're into that.

But I really think this is where all the asymmetric stuff is.

The fun stuff.

If everyone is going one way.

Or if you are.

Maybe you go the other way.

You turn right.

Or left.

Not all the time, now.

All the time gets you in trouble.

Just enough.

To keep things interesting.

Keep things fresh.

If all you do is digital.

Be a little analog.

And versa vice.

All you do is highways.

Take the local route.

Like Bob Frost said.

Take the road less traveled.

Makes all the difference.

Start making orthogonal bets.

Don't make it the main thing.

Unless you want to.

Just enough to be unreasonable.

Within reason.

"Are you going to help me or not?"

"Alright, alright, alright!

I'll tell you what to do:

Go that way.

Really fast.

If something gets in your way,

Turn."

⛷

👈

[Watching you ragdoll down a mountain].

Alright!

Now, turn!!!

🎩

items.title: September And Everything After
items.summary: Time's so interesting. How interesting is it? I'll look back at…
items.content_html:
Time's so interesting.

How interesting is it?

I'll look back at something I thought I've had for years and we bought it in March.

Our "newest" ride has now been with us for almost a decade.

Feels like five years.

Six max.

You might say that's close enough.

But it's not.

It flew.

And sometimes it doesn't.

It lounges.

I like to say "I can't remember my life before..."

And I mean this life.

Now, of course I can.

I can remember it.

But I cannot feel it.

Not the same way.

Not like I used to.

I know I did it.

I know I lived it.

But it just feels like a memory.

Like a first person perspective movie.

Just something I watched happen.

Or played through.

Where am I going with this?

Who knows.

Who ever knows.

Sometimes, I rhyme slow.

Sometimes, I rhyme quick.

🎤

Time rhymes.

Some of the time.

And I know poetry doesn't have to.

But I sure do love it when it does.

You didn't rhyme.

Do.

Ok, it's time.

To decades in seconds.

And the longest hours.

And everything after.

items.title: Sugar Pie Honey Bunches of Hall and Oat(e)s
items.summary: We live in a world, now more than ever, where if…
items.content_html:
We live in a world, now more than ever, where if it sounds too good to be true.

It probably is.

Too good to be true.

Which is a weird, almost positive, way to say it's not true.

And sure, we all encounter that on a daily basis.

Hourly basis.

Minutely basis.

We're unable now to trust our eyes and ears.

If we ever were.

I think it started with those filters that dewrinkled you.

Smoothed it out.

Made you purty(ish).

Now it don't even have to be you.

You just tell it to be.

And it is.

Magic.

I think you can still trust smells.

Touches.

Tastes.

For now.

But see and hear?

Untrustable.

Now, you should always trust your sixth sense.

If you got one.

I used to think everyone did.

But they don't.

Your spidey sense.

If that sheet tingles, you always trust it.

That sheet tapping quantum.

But to me, that means we got three senses left.

Four tops.

Great band.

Or maybe it means we gotta develop new senses.

Hunches.

Trust those.

Inner voices.

Like me.

Trust those (kinda).

Hey!

And your heart.

Aww.

These things.

These senses.

Will let you down.

Sure, like all things.

But it's also important to know that it will let you up.

And that's where I'm going.

So come on up, too.

Always room up here.

Actually.

Ackchyually.

I can't go for that.

No can do.

Pick another mountain.

This one is out of touch.

Haha, can't help myself.

🔊

Soul really matters to me.

Too much.

items.title: Like A Sumo
items.summary: I'm getting kinda fat. There I said it. Dad bod. My…
items.content_html:
I'm getting kinda fat.

There I said it.

Dad bod.

My older (younger) body liked nay loved the iron.

This newer (oldish) body don't.

It just don't.

It likes aluminum.

Lined bags.

Filled with Doritos.

Awful.

Yummy.

Just awful.

The older, younger, body let me down.

Sure, it was fast(ish).

Strong(ish).

But it broke down.

Left me by the side of the road.

Almost totaled.

Almost.

Sure, it could lift more than 225 over my head for reps (seated military) but that strength means nothing if you deed.

If you deed.

Now I lift aluminum cans.

Much lighter weights.

More reps.

Counter to lips.

Over and over.

Not the healthiest way to do things.

It's just coke zero. No beers.

But I'm here to do things.

Not deed.

And the best part of having this new, old(ish), fattish body is that it comes with this brain, man.

This brain thinks differently.

These eyes see with different lenses.

And this heart feels fuller, somehow.

Maybe that's where all the muscle went.

So thankful.

So grateful.

So blessed.

To be getting fat.

Insane.

"Fat boy on a diet.

Don't try it."

items.title: Booth Or Tablet
items.summary: If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a…
items.content_html:
If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a booth.

Huh?

Like say you called me up.

How the heck they get this number?

I don't answer.

I don't see it.

You leave voicemail.

I get to it eventually.

We set up a lunch.

I pick a booth.

That's where I like to mentor.

A booth.

Tables aren't it.

I'm a booth guy.

Can't mentor at a table.

Or a tablet.

📱

Maybe you can.

Of course, I don't mentor.

I'm retired.

Ohhh, that's why.

I don't like that word.

So let's call me secluded.

I'm secluded.

Where was I?

Oh, yes, mentorsheet.

When I did, I notice looking back that they were all in booths.

Mostly in booths.

Might have been a table once or twice.

I'm not a guy who stands up and talks to a crowd and owns the room.

I don't do that.

I'm a guy who booths.

I can own a booth.

Or used to.

A guy who owned booths.

Booth owner.

I think they call it introverted.

But I'm just outroverted.

🍽

So, why am I sitting here?

Did you order apps?

Where's my two coke zeros?

You put anything in this?

Smells funny.

Get a pitcher of zero.

Work on that.

I gotta use the can.

This man walking around here like he's Ray Kroc.
